claims.claim: Redirect URIs must use HTTPS (not HTTP); no raw IP or googleusercontent.com; shorteners disallowed unless you own domain
claims.quote: For testing, you can specify URIs that refer to the local machine, such as http://localhost:8080.
claims.correction: HTTPS required except localhost (incl. localhost IP) URIs, which may use http; raw IP hosts disallowed except localhost IPs; googleusercontent.com host disallowed; shortener domains disallowed unless app owns domain (then path must contain /google-callback/ or end with /google-callback). Also: no wildcards, no fragments, no userinfo, no path traversal, no open redirects. Table rules are paraphrase only (tool would not reproduce verbatim); the localhost quote is verbatim.

claims.claim: U: localhost/http exceptions unknown
claims.quote: For testing, you can specify URIs that refer to the local machine, such as http://localhost:8080.
claims.correction: Can now be verified: localhost http URIs are allowed (and exempt from HTTPS/raw-IP rules) for Web application clients.

missing: Redirect URI rules beyond HTTPS/IP/shortener: no wildcards, no fragments, no userinfo, no path traversal, no open redirects; top-level domain must be on the public suffix list (web-server page).

Calendar API auth page lists 20 scopes incl. Calendar add-on scopes (calendar.addons.execute, addons.current.event.read/write) that the scopes page's 17 omit; and the page says the Cloud Console labels each scope non-sensitive/sensitive/restricted, so the developer can read classification there (support.google.com/cloud/answer/13463073).

Apps using only non-sensitive scopes do not need OAuth verification but may do lighter brand verification for name/logo (support.google.com/cloud/answer/13463073, paraphrase only); and refresh tokens are valid until revoked or expired (web-server page).
